# Introduction

## Background

Globally, extreme weather events such as floods, coldwaves and heatwaves are on the rise. These extreme weather events are associated with a myriad of challenges in diverse fields such as in energy infrastructure, service delivery, agriculture and food production, healthcare, and in people's livelihoods, labour and work due to distress, which in turn lead to economic losses[@costello2009].

Global average near-surface temperatures have increased by approximately $1.4$ to $1.5$ degrees celsius above pre-industrial levels (1850-1900)[@adriansimmons2021]. The five-year average temperatures in the period 2020-2025 were recorded to be the highest on record, 2024 being the hottest year ever. This worsening situation is associated with the increased emission of Green House Gases (GHGs) over time, coupled with atmospheric and oceanic processes[@change2022; @adriansimmons2021].

The rise in surface temperatures often lead to the occurence of heateaves defined as unusually high temperatures extending over a number of days.

The intensity and frequency of heatwaves is predicted to increase, unless measures are taken across all regions towards reducing GHG emissions, and strengthening infrastructure.

In healthcare, heatwaves have been associated with health system challenges such as in the storage of vaccines, medical equipments and drugs[@curtis2017; @carmichael2012], increase in heat related injury particularly among the elderly[@hajat2007], prolonged recovery by patients and an increase in in-patient mortality[@ferron2006; @stafoggia2008], and general excess mortality in several regions globally[@hundessa2025; @clarke2025; @he].

Heatwaves have also been associated with mental health conditions due to sleep disruption,

Nigeria has experienced heatwaves in the recent past with a 2019 and 2020 heatwave being the most profound. The heatwaves are due to localized climates, and are intense in urban areas with a huge number of concrete structures and fewer vegetation, the heatwaves are also as a result of deforestation, and the expansion of urban centers,

These heatwaves have led to reduced agricultural output which have further led to economic losses, and threat to food security in regions such as Northern Nigeria, straining of the energy infrastructure due to increased demand for cooling, an increase in heat related illnesses such as menengitis and stroke and mortality and a loss of productivity in the workforce.
